title_original: ‘They’re Still Humans Like the Rest of Us’: Watch the ‘Everest: The Other Side’ Directors Discuss Relating to Extreme Athletes
excerpt_original: At IndieWire's Art of the Doc event, Elizabeth Chai Vasarhelyi and Jimmy Chin explained what draws them to some of the world's biggest risk-takers.

blocks.text: Elizabeth Chai Vasarhelyi and Jimmy Chin know a thing or two about extreme athletes. From the daring rock climbing of “Free Solo” to their new film “Everest: The Other Side,” which follows Jim Morrison’s attempts to fulfill his late wife Hilaree Nelson’s dream of skiing down the world’s tallest mountain, the documentarians love to capture fearless people drawn to extreme challenges.

During a conversation about “Everest” with IndieWire features writer Alison Foreman at our Art of the Doc event in Los Angeles, the filmmakers discussed what draws them to the subject matter over and over again.

“In all our films, you think you’re seeing these exceptional, extraordinary, extreme athletes. But at the end of the day they’re still human beings like the rest of us,” Chin said. “What I’m interested in bridging that gap where people feel like they can’t relate to people out there doing these things. But the story is really human, and this film is about very human experiences. Even though they’re climbing and skiiing the most extreme places in the world.”

blocks.text: Vasarhelyi also emphasized the fact that each documentary subject is a different person with their own unique story to tell. In the case of Nelson, she saw someone who was deeply goal-oriented but lacked the grand romanticizations about her sport that drive so many other athletes. She saw the adventurer as a fellow parent who lived a fairly normal life when she wasn’t pushing herself to scale the world’s highest peaks.

“I had met a lot of extreme athletes, but Hilaree had a candor to her vocation that I hadn’t heard before,” Vasarhelyi said. “It’s not romantic. She says in the film, ‘I know it’s just a mountain, but it’s everything to me. And I’m like a dog with a bone.’ And I understand that.”
National Geographic will release “Everest: The Other Side” in theaters on Friday, October 30. Watch the complete conversation in the video above.
